Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required wake-visual skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring histories.

The visual-first skill requires anchoring the images to observations and metrics, then comparing the best finite result with the most informative failure. I’m gathering those records, inherited notes, and the assigned-parent guidance now; the candidate file will remain untouched and non-empty until the diagnosis is written.

The sampled records already separate three mechanisms: the seed was swept downward while saturated; a low-effort slow controller was carried downstream; and the strongest finite controller moved upstream with bounded target steering but overshot above the target before exiting. I’m checking those interpretations against the keyframe sheets now, including the common prewarm and the unstable-load failure.

The images confirm the key distinction. The strongest policy genuinely self-propels into the developed wake and cuts its distance roughly in half, but its target turn grows into a wide loop and top-boundary exit; the slow negative-sign variant turns sharply the wrong way almost immediately, while the unstable variant folds into a high-load curl before any useful approach. I’ll now map the legal body-frame observations and actuator conventions so the new feedback stays within the public contract.

I’m recording the required pre-edit diagnosis now. The candidate hypothesis is a conservative repair of the strongest sampled controller: retain its proven positive target-steering sign and 0.90-period propulsion, keep steering out of the anterior oscillator, but add bounded bearing-rate lead and modestly reduce gait/tail authority to arrest the observed loop and saturation.

The policy and durable lesson are now updated. The reusable lesson records both the positive mechanism and its boundary: positive posterior-only target steering improved approach, but P-only saturation looped; negative-sign steering and anterior-equilibrium steering are current avoid cases. I’m doing contract/schema checks next, without running CFD.

The candidate is non-empty, uses only documented state fields, and every `params.FIELD` reference is present in `target_policy_params()`. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the dedicated no-CFD check runner for the guidance semantic check, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary check.
